Summary: New in this pass: home air-purifier, humidifier and water-filter brands sold D2C (Mila, Rabbit Air, Canopy, Clearly Filtered, LARQ). Molekule was excluded as defunct. No recent category-level figure was confirmed.

D2C-plus-retail auto accessories and car care (WeatherTech, TuxMat, Chemical Guys, Crutchfield) are included. Marketplace-style truck-part retailers were excluded. No recent category financials were used.

Adobe projects holiday 2026 baby-product online sales 113% above average September levels during Cyber Week, but that is a seasonal spike, not a full-year rate. The Honest Company's FY2025 revenue fell 1.9% and 2026 reported revenue is guided down 16–18% after category exits; most other baby/kids brands here are Unclear.

eMarketer says food and beverage will propel US ecommerce in 2026, while holiday data also shows cosmetics among the faster categories: Adobe projects online cosmetics up about 10% in holiday 2026. e.l.f. Beauty's latest-year revenue rose 24.6% to $1.6B and it acquired Rhode; Olaplex and Beauty Health (Hydrafacial) declined.

The list now includes major US e-bike and D2C bike brands (Rad Power, Aventon, Lectric, Super73, Priority). The post-2021 e-bike boom cooled, but no 2025–2026 category figure was confirmed, so the trend is Unclear rather than assumed down.

Adobe expects holiday 2026 online electronics sales of $63.3B, up 5.9%. Peloton's Q4 FY2025 sales were down ~6% but FY2026 was guided at $2.4–$2.5B with $320M FY2025 free cash flow; other connected-fitness and gadget brands here are mostly Unclear.
Cricut is the public anchor in this small group, alongside Knit Picks and Purl Soho. No FY2025/FY2026 Cricut figure was used in this pass.
Warby Parker, the anchor brand, reported FY2025 revenue of $872M, up 13.0%. Other online eyewear brands in the list had no recent public filings in this pass.
Accessory-led brands such as Baggu, Cuyana, Ridge and Pela are broken out separately from apparel and luggage, and no recent public financials were found for them.

Adobe expects US holiday 2026 online apparel sales of $51.3B, up 4.7%. In this list, Quince, FIGS, Rent the Runway and workwear brand BRUNT show clear growth, Lululemon is only modestly up with lower operating profit, and many digitally native apparel brands have no recent public filings.
Farm-direct and on-demand florists (UrbanStems, The Bouqs, Farmgirl Flowers) plus gift brands (Uncommon Goods) are now grouped here. No recent category-level financials were used.

eMarketer (Mar 2026) says food and beverage will be the main engine of a US ecommerce rebound through 2030. Adobe also projects holiday 2026 online grocery up about 10% to $26.1B. Meat snacks, candy and other shelf-stable snacks are now broken out in a separate Snacks & Meat Snacks tab row.
The category is mixed. Allbirds' FY2025 revenue fell 19.7% and it agreed in Mar 2026 to sell brand/IP for ~$39M, while many other D2C footwear labels in the list have no recent public filings.
Houseplant and seed D2C (The Sill, Bloomscape, Lettuce Grow, Johnny's) is established online, but no reliable 2025–2026 category growth figure was confirmed in this pass.

Hims & Hers' FY2025 revenue rose 59% to $2.3B, and the category is subscription-friendly. Broader US ecommerce commentary still treats wellness/supplements as a resilient online vertical, though most private supplement brands in this list are Unclear.

Premium artificial-tree DTC (Balsam Hill, King of Christmas, Treetopia) is a large seasonal online category, but no reliable full-year 2025–2026 category growth figure was confirmed in this pass, and unsourced market-share estimates were not used.

Adobe forecasts holiday 2026 online furniture sales up 7.3% to $33.4B, but mattress DTC is weaker: Purple's latest-year revenue fell 3.9% with a -9.2% operating margin, and Casper remains private after its 2022 take-private with no recent public figures.

Adobe expects household cleaning to rise 49% vs average September sales during Cyber Week, but that is seasonal. No full-year 2026 category financials were used, and brands such as Blueland, Grove and Tru Earth are Unclear at the brand level.

The list includes Mejuri, Gorjana, Kendra Scott and online diamond retailers, but no reliable 2025–2026 category-level ecommerce growth figure was confirmed in this pass, and brand-level filings were not reviewed in depth.

New grill, coffee-equipment and appliance brands (Traeger, Blackstone, Fellow, Mill, Lomi) are listed here. Earlier cookware entries such as Made In, HexClad, Caraway and Our Place remain under Home & Furniture so historical rows were not rewritten. Traeger is public; no FY2025/FY2026 figure was used.
Harry's, Dollar Shave Club and Dr. Squatch are established, but no recent public brand-level growth figures were found in this pass (Harry's is inside Edgewell; DSC is inside Unilever).

This group covers fire pits, coolers, camp stoves and ultralight gear (Solo Stove, BioLite, RTIC, NEMO, Big Agnes). Yeti remains in Travel & Luggage. No recent category-level ecommerce figure was used.
Online party and invitation specialists (Oriental Trading, Shindigz, Basic Invite) are included. Party City-style mall retail was not added. No recent category financials were used.

Adobe flags pet among holiday essential categories (Cyber Week pet sales 93% above September averages). Results in this list are mixed: Chewy's FY2025 revenue rose 6.2% to $12.6B and operating profit more than doubled, while Bark fell 18.5% and PetMed Express fell 21.1%.
NA D2C and omnichannel brands (Dame, Maude, We-Vibe, Foria, OhNut) are listed. No reliable recent category-level ecommerce figure was used.

Protein snacks sit inside the broader grocery/F&B online upswing, but the only public brand newly added here, Stryve (OTC: SNAX), expected roughly flat FY2025 revenue, a still-negative net loss, a strategic-alternatives review, and a January 2026 production halt after plant damage. Most other snack brands are Unclear.

Golf (Newton Golf, formerly Sacks Parente; L.A.B. Golf; PXG), pickleball (Selkirk), ergs (Concept2) and garage-gym brands are grouped here. Rogue and REP remain under Consumer Electronics. Seed Golf was excluded as Ireland-founded.
Notebook, planner and desk brands (Ugmonk, Field Notes, Rifle Paper Co., Erin Condren, Grovemade) are grouped here. No 2025–2026 category figure was confirmed.

New in this pass: curated subscription and gifting boxes (Ipsy, FabFitFun, Causebox, Bespoke Post, Book of the Month, Literati, Universal Yums, Bokksu, Atlas Coffee Club, Sugarwish). Meal kits and single-product subscriptions stay under their product categories. No recent category-level figure was confirmed, so the trend is Unclear.

True D2C power-tool specialists are scarce versus traditional trade brands. This group is mostly hand tools, woodworking and multi-tools (Lee Valley, Lie-Nielsen, Tekton, Leatherman, Woodpeckers, Kreg). No category-level 2026 figure was used.

Adobe's holiday 2026 forecast pegs US online toy sales at about $9.6B, up roughly 10%. This new group includes KiwiCo, Magna-Tiles, Melissa & Doug and game studios such as Exploding Kittens; Lovevery remains listed under Baby & Kids. No brand-level FY2025/FY2026 figures were used here.

Yeti, the largest public brand in this group, posted FY2025 revenue of $1.9B, up just 2.1%, with operating profit down 13%. Away, Monos, Béis and others lack recent public financials, so the category is marked Stable pending better data.
